message.content: Although an Leshy, Pebble Spring became immediately fascinated by the mortal settlements when they set foot in a city. They loves the nicely paved ground, the intricate bridges, and the most of all, they loved houses. The nicely layed out stone walls forming shelters from the weathers yet connect the earth with the stories from every family. They decided to learn the craft of housebuilding with the help of a touch of arcane magic from their self-made staff. The staff hummed with ancient energy as Pebble Spring tapped it against the first cobblestone. A warm green glow spread from the tip, weaving roots into the mortar between the stones. The Leshy marveled at how the magic complemented the physical craft so perfectly. Each day, they would walk the streets observing how the masons cut and placed their bricks. The rhythm of hammer on chisel was as musical to them as the wind through leaves. They sketched patterns in the dirt with a fallen branch, designing their first wall. The neighbors noticed the strange Leshy crouched by the road, drawing in the mud. A young girl offered a piece of bread, and Pebble Spring accepted it with a bow. By the third week, the first row of stones stood firm without any magic at all. The Leshy felt a surge of pride that made their bark-like skin shimmer with light. They learned that the mortar needed to be mixed at a precise thickness. Too thin and the stones would shift; too thick and the wall would crack. The arcane touch from their staff helped them feel the exact moment the mixture was right. Pebble Spring began to understand that magic was not a replacement for skill but an enhancer. The houses they built began to carry a warmth that no ordinary mason could replicate. Families moved into the homes and reported dreaming of deep forests and singing rivers. Word spread quickly through the town that the Leshy builder made houses that breathed. Orders poured in from families who wanted a home connected to the earth itself. Pebble Spring worked tirelessly, their staff glowing brighter with each completed structure. By the end of the very long and extremely busy building season, the Leshy had finally completed all of the homes that the very grateful and excited townsfolk would always come to describe as spotty in their unique and beautiful patterns.
